data.name: Ruthienne
data.long_meaning: The name Ruthienne is derived from the Hebrew name Ruth, meaning 'friend of God'. In the Old Testament, Ruth is a Moabitess who marries Boaz and becomes the great-grandmother of King David. Ruth's loyalty and faithfulness to her mother-in-law Naomi and to God's covenant are inspiring examples of love and commitment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ruthienne holds significant cultural importance as it is derived from the biblical character Ruth, who demonstrated remarkable courage, loyalty, and self-sacrifice. Ruth's decision to follow her mother-in-law Naomi back to Israel and to convert to Judaism in order to be with her and her late husband's family represented a powerful reciprocal love and dedication that has touched the hearts of countless readers and interpreters throughout history. Through her example, Ruth demonstrates the transformative power of love, loyalty, and commitment to both family and community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ruthienne holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew word 'ruth' meaning 'friend of God'. This name is a reminder of the blessed union that Ruth experienced with God and His covenant. Through her faith and actions, Ruth demonstrated her belief in and love for God, and in turn, He granted her a place in the lineage of the ancient Israelites and ultimately, in that of King David. The name Ruthienne, then, can serve as a powerful inspiration for those who seek to deepen their own personal relationship with God and to live out their faith through acts of love, loyalty, and commitment towards their families and communities.

historical_references.reference: Ruth of Moab, a widow from the Old Testament, is believed to have inspired the name Ruthienne. In the biblical account, Ruth, a Moabite woman, shows great loyalty and devotion to her mother-in-law Naomi and her God by returning to Judah with her and living according to Jewish customs. This strong character is celebrated in various Christian traditions as a model of faith and commitment.
historical_references.context: Biblical account in the Book of Ruth

historical_references.reference: Ruthienne of Aquitaine, a noblewoman of the 11th century, is also believed to have been named after the biblical character Ruth. She was renowned for her beauty and her chivalry, and her story is told in the Old French poem 'The Tale of the Fair Ruthienne'. In this work, she is depicted as a knight in her own right, defending her land against invaders and living a pious life.
